subject: Hosted API competitive rate teardown & matching request
messages:
From: Priya Rao <pricing@novamart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novamart.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Hosted API rate teardown (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Novamart is keen to understand the unit economics for Redwood's hosted API compared to the public rates we can find for OpenAI, Anthropic, Together, and AWS. We're running a multi-workload forecast (chat + embeddings + occasional long-form generation) and need a baseline table to present to procurement.

Could you: 
- Share a simple rate teardown (per 1k tokens / per-embedding) and any volume breakpoints you commonly use.
- Call out differences for streaming vs non-streaming and any extra per-request overheads.
- Indicate what discounts or packaging you can offer for a committed monthly spend in the $40k–$80k range and whether dedicated capacity is relevant.

I've attached a short usage summary and example prompt mix. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Priya Rao
Procurement Lead, Novamart Retail
pricing@novamart.com

Attachment: novamart_usage_summary.csv (csv stub, 3 rows)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <pricing@novamart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Hosted API rate teardown (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS)

Hi Priya — thanks for the usage file and the clear ask. Appreciate the context. 

High level: we can absolutely put together a compact teardown and a matching proposal for the $40k–$80k committed monthly band. To keep it useful for procurement, we'll provide:
- A baseline per-1k-token hosted rate for our standard model family (gen-mid), plus a comparison row showing public list pricing we pulled for OpenAI/GPT, Anthropic/Claude, Together, and AWS Bedrock.
- Embedding unit rates and guidance on typical dimensionality/throughput costs.
- Notes on streaming vs non-streaming overhead and a small appendix on KV cache savings for chat sessions.
- Two packaging options: (A) Hosted pay-as-you-go with a staged volume discount ladder, (B) 6/12-month committed hosted credit with a committed discount + canary dedicated pool add-on.

Ben — looping you in for the detailed numbers and the suggested commercial. Evelyn — flagging for any one-off approval thresholds (we may propose an introductory 20% credit for the first quarter to win live traffic).

Can we get the teardown to them by EOD Wednesday 11/4? If Novamart wants firm competitor public-rate citations, Ben will attach the quick reference sheet.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first LLM serving

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Priya Rao <pricing@novamart.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@novamart.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Hosted API rate teardown (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS)

Priya, Jordan — attached is a concise reference table and the public citations I used. Highlights up front:
- Redwood hosted baseline (gen-mid): $0.60 / 1k tokens (generation) / $0.03 / 1k tokens (prompt) — streaming carries a marginal per-request charge that averages out to ~$0.02 / request for our observed prompt sizes.
- Embeddings (base-embed): $0.006 per 1k embedding-units (we price by 1k vectors here; we can map to Novamart's vector size if you send dims).
- Public list rates captured: OpenAI GPT-4/4o-ish equivalent public list approximate, Anthropic Claude estimates, Together unit tiers, AWS Bedrock per-request proxies. See competitor_public_rates.xlsx.

Commercial options we recommend:
1) Committed hosted (12-month): 12% discount at $40k/mo, 18% at $60k/mo, 25% at $80k/mo + 30-day rolling true-up. Includes basic SSO + audit logs.
2) Short-term win (quarter): 20% first-quarter credit to offset migration costs; standard usage rates thereafter.
3) Dedicated add-on: add a canary dedicated pool for predictable latency (+ fixed $8k/mo) — recommended if >70% chat traffic.

Notes on parity requests: we are happy to match a documented public list if a comparable usage profile and contract term are provided, but we do not match undisclosed enterprise discounts. To proceed to a formal match we need: (a) recent invoice or reseller proof of the competitor rate, (b) an expected commit, and (c) a short SOW for data controls if dedicated is requested.

I've attached redwood_ratecard_v3.pdf and competitor_public_rates.xlsx. Jordan — please confirm if you want me to propose the 20% intro credit for this deal.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_ratecard_v3.pdf (pdf stub)
Attachment: competitor_public_rates.xlsx (xlsx stub)
